Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 4 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: deus -> (absent from the aligned window); offenderis penitentia placaris preces populi -> off nderis penit ntia plac ris pre ces p puli; flagella tue iracundie -> flag a tiue iracundiai; peccatis -> pec cdtis; 1922 Mame text layer damages 2 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): deus -> (absent from the aligned window); iracundie -> iracundiz; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 75, artifact PDF p. 189; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 26310 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer. Recorded limitation: The day was identified by the facsimile's own running head (Feria V post cineres) and by the station heading that opens the formulary, and this oration is the first Oratio the Missal prints inside that day's Mass, taken after that day's Ant. ad Introitum and before the next day's station heading; the marginal number was read on the page image. Every 1862 reading in this entry rests on that book's whole-book text layer alone - this repository holds no page images for its temporal run - so where that layer damages a word the letterforms are inferred from the 1922 Mame at the same place rather than read. The 1862's own locus for this day scores only 0.55 on a token-level alignment; every difference behind that score is recogniser damage (accents dropped, words split at line breaks, running heads and the scan's watermark intruding), not a different petition. Not checked: the Oratio super populum that the 1962 prints after this Mass's Postcommunion (not on this work list), the 1604 and the 1570, and whether the 1862 also prints this prayer elsewhere in its book.

propers.text:
Deus, qui culpa offenderis, paenitentia placaris: preces populi tui
supplicantis propitius respice; et flagella tuae iracundiae, quae pro
peccatis nostris meremur, averte. Per Dominum.

translations.caution: Original study translation; not approved for liturgical use or recitation.
translations.text: God, whom sin offends and penance appeases, look favorably upon the prayers of your people who plead with you, and turn away the scourges of your anger that we deserve for our sins. Through the Lord.
